name: Catching Wind

angles.text: Shamans may find themselves torn between the Windshapers' reverence for the elemental currents and the High Order's clinical extraction of raw elemental power.
Arcane scholars and mages appreciate the analytical function of the Index Esoteria, treating elemental phenomena as measurable fields of arcane research.

faq.answer: Catching Wind is a mission undertaken on behalf of the High Order to study the elemental energy around the Overlook Standing Stones in the Shen'dar Highlands. An adventurer is tasked with carrying an Index Esoteria to extract vital data from massive windstone formations despite hostile pushback from the Windshapers.
faq.q: What is the quest Catching Wind about?

faq.answer: The Index Esoteria is a specialized measuring instrument utilized by the High Order. It is designed to extract, measure, and record elemental energy data directly from massive windstone formations found at the Overlook Standing Stones.

The Windshapers are a faction fiercely protective of their sacred sites and traditional beliefs regarding elemental magic. They view the High Order's scholarly research and technological devices as desecration, aggressively defending the windstone formations from outside intrusion.

The Al'Aketh are an overtly violent group mentioned by the High Order alongside the Windshapers. The High Order says the Al'Aketh are the more overtly violent of the two, but views both factions as dangerous zealots bound to misplaced, inflexible dogmas.

The Overlook Standing Stones are located within the Shen'dar Highlands. The site is notable for housing massive windstone formations that channel strong elemental currents, making it a critical research location for the High Order.
faq.q: Where are the Overlook Standing Stones located?

faq.answer: Fillion is an operative or researcher of the High Order who was originally dispatched to the Overlook Standing Stones to measure and study the elemental energy. Confrontation with the Windshapers necessitated sending an adventurer with the Index Esoteria to secure the data.

aliases: why does high order want data
faq.answer: The High Order believes that understanding the elemental forces of the realm is critical to their overarching mission to save Zephras. They view scientific inquiry as essential to overcoming elemental threats that traditional beliefs cannot resolve.
faq.q: Why does the High Order need the windstone data?

sections.body: The High Order seeks to measure and understand the chaotic elemental flows coursing through the Shen'dar Highlands. To unlock the secrets held within the Overlook Standing Stones, researchers crafted the Index Esoteria, a precision tool intended to extract data from massive windstone formations. While the High Order frames their work as vital research necessary to save Zephras, local traditionalists interpret these academic probes as profane trespasses against the wind.
sections.title: Measuring the Gales

sections.body: Tensions quickly ignite at the stones between the High Order's expedition and the Windshapers. The Windshapers view the study and extraction of elemental energies as an outright desecration of their sacred traditions. The High Order considers the Windshapers to be as dogmatically narrow-minded as the violent Al'Aketh, refusing to let indigenous resistance halt their mission to save the realm.
sections.title: Clash of Dogma and Inquiry

sections.body: When the High Order's work at the Overlook Standing Stones meets hostile resistance, force becomes inevitable. The resulting clash leaves blood spilled among the windstones. While the High Order successfully secures their readings with the Index Esoteria, the Windshapers decry the incident as a massacre, intensifying a bitter feud that shadows the city of Valanaar.
sections.title: The Standing Stone Massacre

summary: Catching Wind is a High Order expedition to the Overlook Standing Stones in the Shen'dar Highlands. Armed with an Index Esoteria, an operative is sent to extract elemental energy readings from ancient windstone formations over the fierce, violent objections of the traditionalist Windshapers.
